messages.author: ab6dbc67ee8c01b4
messages.subject: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
parts:
Hello Francesco, 

I would normally post on the Google Group for support, but I'm working on a project that is time-sensitive and wished to contact you directly to expedite the process. I've requested to join the group and as soon as you accept my request, I'll post my question and associated answers there for posterity. 

I'm trying to run bam2seqz on exome tumour-normal pairs, because we don't generate large mpileup files as part of our standard pipeline and this simplifies the process. However, I'm been running into an issue where bam2seqz stalls towards the end of processing the BAM files. Using samtools mpileup and pileup2seqz approach, I obtain a 760-MB gzipped SEQZ file. Using the bam2seqz, the gzipped SEQZ file stops growing at ~731 MB. Strangely, the bam2seqz process doesn't exit, nor outputs any errors. 

The problem mentioned in this thread sounded similar to mine. So, I tried using pypy instead, but came to the same result. 

While writing this, I though I should test the same pipeline on a different tumour-normal pair to verify if the problem lies with Sequenza or my environment as opposed to a corrupted file. I'll let you know how this goes. This being said, I don't understand why bam2seqz would get stalled, but running mpileup and pileup2seqz separately would work. The only difference between the two I can think of is the use of named pipes in bam2seqz. I don't have much experience with them, so maybe you can identify potential explanations that would account for my weird issue. 

In case it would help, here's the command I'm running:

$LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/software/pypy-4.0.1/bin/pypy $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/software/R-3.2.1/lib/R/library/sequenza/exec/sequenza-utils.py bam2seqz --tumor $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/data/LS1065.bam -gc $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/reference/GRCh37.gc50Base.txt.gz --normal $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/data/LS1065N.bam --fasta $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/reference/Homo_sapiens_assembly19_EBV.fasta --samtools $LOHR_PROJECT_HOME/software/samtools/1.2/iuc/package_samtools_1_2/6eea04363026/bin/samtools | gzip > 1-bam2seqz/LS1065.seqz.gz

I appreciate any help! I'll be sure to post this to the Google Group as soon as I can. Thanks, Francesco! 

Cheers, 
Bruno

messages.author: ab6dbc67ee8c01b4
messages.subject: Re: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
parts:
Francesco responded with the following by email:

Hi Bruno,
I'll immediately have a look at the google group account for granting access (I thought it was public, but I'll check ).
Can it be that either the chromosomes have a different order either in the 2 bams or in the gc file?
In bam2seqz, when you have indexed bams, you can run the code on a subsection of the bam with the -c/--chromosome option.
I usually run each chromosome separately and then merge the results.
Doing that it would overcome a sorting issues, if one of the three file is "wrong"... And it would also complete in a shorter time.
Please don't hesitate to write me back, and let me know it this solve e the problem.
Best
Francesco

parts:
Hello Francesco, 

Under normal circumstances, I would parallelize the various chromosomes to speed up the analysis. However, my current task demands that I run the pipeline sequentially (i.e. non-parallelized). 

Upon inspection of the BAM, FASTA and GC content files, I noticed that the first two contain an extra contig at the end that isn't in the GC content file: NC_007605 (human herpesvirus 4). Would this explain the issue I'm running into? If so, why would the issue only arise with bam2seqz, but not with running mpileup and pileup2seqz separately?

Cheers, 
Bruno

messages.author: dad6980b76d10753
messages.subject: Re: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
parts:
The extra contigs should not have an impact, unless it is in between other common chromosomes (I think this would cause to skip every chromosomes after that point, but the script would still run until all the chromosomes are processed).

Are you sure the process is stalling, or is it possible taht is finishing to process the various bams? (withoit finiding any common position)... As a result of the above mentioned situation).

Alternatively, it could be something about the pypy version, I've never tried version 4. The only difference between the pileup2seqz and the bam2seqz is an intermediate fifo grneration (samtools mpileup output in named queues). Could you try with python2.7 (yeah, I know, it's slow)

I find it odd that pileup2seqz works and bam2seqz doesn't.

messages.author: ab6dbc67ee8c01b4
messages.subject: Re: bam2seqz stalls without errors or exiting
parts:
Hello all, 

I wanted to post my workaround for others who stumble on this thread. 

My admittedly short-term solution was to omit all small chromosomes that have a small number of mapped reads. For humans, this meant that I only included chromosomes 1 through 22 and X in my copy number analysis, which I deemed reasonable. I tried including the Y chromosome, but occasionally ran into this issue, presumably with samples from female patients. You may be able to include Y for males, if you have that information. 

In doing so, I ran into a bug with Sequenza where one cannot specify more than one region (e.g. multiple chromosomes) with the --chromosome argument in bam2seqz. Francesco merged a pull request last month that included a fix for this, but it hasn't made it into a versioned release yet. So, if you are to restrict Sequenza to only run on the major chromosomes, you'll have to use sequenza-utils.py from the latest commit from the master branch on BitBucket. For the R analysis, you can still use what's on CRAN. 

Francesco, do you have any plans on releasing a minor version bump with the bug fix? 

I hope this helps others with their analyses!

Cheers, 
Bruno
